question: Show that $$\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{13}\right)=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{12}{5}\right).$$
explanation:
Assignment of the inverse cosine angle
Let $$\theta=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{13}\right).$$ Since the argument is positive, $\theta\in\left(0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$ and $$\cos\theta=\frac{5}{13}.$$

Determination of the sine value
Using $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1$, $$\sin\theta=\sqrt{1-\frac{25}{169}}=\sqrt{\frac{144}{169}}=\frac{12}{13}.$$ The positive root is selected because $\theta$ is acute.

Determination of the tangent value
Therefore, $$\tan\theta=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}=\frac{12/13}{5/13}=\frac{12}{5}.$$

Principal range verification
Since $\theta\in\left(0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$, it lies in the principal range of $\tan^{-1}x$. Hence, $$\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{12}{5}\right).$$

Established result
Thus, $$\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{13}\right)=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{12}{5}\right).$$
